identificationModule.briefTitle: A Study of Neoadjuvant Therapy With BCD-217 (Nurulimab + Prolgolimab) in Patients With Resectable Stage III Skin Melanoma
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Randomized Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Neoadjuvant Therapy With BCD-217 (Nurulimab + Prolgolimab) Versus Standard Adjuvant Therapy With Pembrolizumab in Patients With Resectable Stage III Skin Melanoma.

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This study is an open-label, randomized, comparative phase III study, which will include subjects with resectable stage III skin melanoma (up to 3 resectable transient metastases are acceptable).
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
In both study groups, adjuvant therapy is possible until melanoma progresses to unresectable stage III-IV, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of ICF or the end of the therapy period (12 months).

In case of postoperative relapse of the disease, at the decision of the investigator and if the lesion is resectable, radical surgical treatment can be carried out (R0 - resection) in accordance with current clinical guidelines without withdrawing the patient from the study.

armGroups.label: Subjects with pCR and pnCR (Group 1A)
armGroups.description:
Subjects will receive 2 cycles of BCD-217 neoadjuvant therapy, followed by index lymph node removal.

Subjects with pathological complete (pCR) and near complete response (pnCR) (Group 1A): excision of the primary lesion (if not previously performed) without regional lymphadenectomy, followed by up to 12 months of anti-PD1 agent in the adjuvant setting.
interventionNames: Procedure: Excision of the primary lesion

armGroups.label: Subjects with a pPR or pNR to neoadjuvant therapy (Group 1B)
armGroups.description:
Subjects will receive 2 cycles of BCD-217 neoadjuvant therapy, followed by index lymph node removal.

Subjects with a pathological partial response (pPR) or non-responders (pNR) to neoadjuvant therapy (Group 1B): excision of the primary lesion (if not performed earlier), regional lymphadenectomy, then up to 12 months of adjuvant therapy with anti-PD1 agent.
interventionNames: Procedure: Excision of the primary lesion

armGroups.label: Control Group (Group 2)
armGroups.description: Subjects start treatment with excision of the primary lesion (if not previously performed), regional lymphadenectomy followed by adjuvant therapy with anti-PD1 agent (up to 12 months). This approach is considered the standard therapy for patients in the target population.
interventionNames: Procedure: Excision of the primary lesion
